title: Step 2: Add per-market verified HTTP fetch methods with strict allowlist + fix deploy-breaking actor API mismatch

requirements.text: In `backend/main.mo`, add four dedicated **backend update methods** to fetch external market data by category—one each for **crypto**, **stocks**, **fiat**, and **commodities**—implemented as separate functions (not a single generic fetch). Each method must perform verified HTTPS outcalls using the existing `OutCall.httpGetRequest(..., transform)` pattern and return the raw response text (or a structured error via trap) for now.

quotes: please proceed with Step 2: Add individual endpoint fetch functions (crypto, stocks, fiat, commodities) with safe verified HTTP calls.

acceptanceCriteria: Backend compiles with four separate update methods for crypto/stocks/fiat/commodities external fetches.
Each method uses `OutCall.httpGetRequest(url, [], transform)` and the existing `transform` query method.
Each method is callable via Candid and returns the fetched response body as `Text`.

requirements.text: Implement a strict, hardcoded **HTTPS allowlist** for outbound requests used by the new per-market fetch methods. The backend must reject (trap) any URL that is not explicitly allowlisted, including any non-HTTPS URL. The allowlist may be maintained as one list per market type or a single allowlist keyed by market type, but the per-market methods must only be able to call their own allowlisted endpoints.

quotes: Add individual endpoint fetch functions (crypto, stocks, fiat, commodities) with safe verified HTTP calls.

acceptanceCriteria: Calling a per-market fetch method with a URL not on the allowlist traps with a clear error message.
Calling a per-market fetch method with a non-HTTPS URL traps with a clear error message.
Only the hardcoded allowlisted URLs are reachable; the canister cannot be used as an arbitrary open proxy.

requirements.text: Update or replace the existing `fetchExternalData(url : Text)` backend method so it is no longer a general-purpose arbitrary-URL fetch for normal users. Align it with the same allowlist safety model (e.g., remove it, restrict it to admins, or route it through the same allowlist verification), and ensure the backend Candid interface matches the implemented methods to prevent deploy/interface mismatches.

quotes: Add individual endpoint fetch functions (crypto, stocks, fiat, commodities) with safe verified HTTP calls.

acceptanceCriteria: `fetchExternalData` can no longer successfully fetch arbitrary user-provided URLs.
If `fetchExternalData` remains available, it enforces the same HTTPS + allowlist checks (or is admin-only).
The deployed backend Candid interface includes only the intended public methods and matches the implementation.

requirements.text: Fix the known deployment-blocking backend/frontend actor API mismatch by ensuring the backend exposes a public method matching the frontend initialization call `actor._initializeAccessControlWithSecret(adminToken)` (as documented), or otherwise make the backend initialization compatible **without modifying immutable frontend paths**. After the fix, the backend must deploy and the frontend actor must initialize without runtime errors.

quotes: yes please investigate the issue and try one more time

acceptanceCriteria: Frontend actor initialization no longer throws due to missing `_initializeAccessControlWithSecret`.
No changes are made to immutable frontend paths (including `frontend/src/hooks/useActor.ts`).

constraints: Keep all Motoko logic in the single actor at `backend/main.mo` (no additional backend services).
Do not modify any paths listed in `frontend.immutablePaths` (must resolve compatibility via backend/public API or non-immutable frontend files only).
Outbound HTTP requests must be verified HTTP outcalls and restricted to a hardcoded HTTPS allowlist; do not introduce any open-proxy capability.
nonGoals: UI modernization/design-system changes across the app (out of scope for this Step 2 build).
Adding base currency selection, conversion logic, or dashboard analytics enhancements (not part of Step 2).
Introducing external databases, third-party auth providers, websockets, or additional backend canisters.
